title: China’s Property Crisis: From Evergrande Collapse to Beijing’s Latest Measures
summary: Once one of the country’s biggest growth drivers, China’s property market has been in a downward spiral for five years. Real estate values continue to plummet, households in financial distress are being forced to sell properties, and apartment developers that racked up enormous debt on speculative projects are on the brink of collapse.

title: Gina Rinehart Backed Lynas to Buy Rare Earths Miner Meteoric
summary: Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths Ltd. will acquire Meteoric Resources Ltd. in an all-share deal worth about A$968 million ($672 million), giving it access to a new deposit of the critical minerals in Brazil.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 1
summary: Oil steadied after gaining in the previous session on uncertainty over whether a recovery in Middle East flows can be sustained.

title: Passengers Avert Crash by Tackling Pilot Who Stabbed Colleague
summary:
A pilot of a jet carrying more than 170 passengers to Tel Aviv stabbed his colleague and tried to crash the plane in what Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu branded a serious security incident. Bloomberg's Benedikt Kammel has more.

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Steady as Softer Inflation Data Tempers Fed Rate-Hike Bets
summary: Gold opened the month steady as softer inflation data lowered bets the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next meeting, while high bond yields left the door open to renewed selling.

title: US Stock Futures Advance, Bond Yields in Focus: Markets Wrap
summary: US equity-index futures rose in early Asian trading, steadying sentiment at the start of a new quarter after late swings on Wall Street erased gains sparked by softer-than-expected inflation data.

title: RBI’s Success on Dollar Flows Raises Stakes in Inflation Fight
summary: Just months ago, India’s central bank pulled out all the stops to draw in dollars to bolster its foreign-exchange reserves and defend the rupee. The stronger-than-expected deluge of cash is now adding to the case for a more hawkish monetary policy stance.

title: CFTC Secures $30 Million Judgment Tied to Alleged Crypto Scam
summary: A federal judge in Florida ordered two individuals to pay more than $30 million in restitution and penalties for allegedly defrauding more than 9,000 people in a scam involving crytocurrencies and precious metals, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission said in a statement Wednesdsay.

title: CCC Debt Turns Distressed for First Time Since 2023 Crisis
summary: The spread on the riskiest US corporate bonds has jumped above 1,000 basis points over Treasuries for the first time since the regional banking crisis in 2023. That level of risk premium typically implies high probability of default, restructuring or loss.

title: Hedge Funds Diameter, Redwood Bought Nuveen Brightline Debt
summary: Distressed-debt hedge funds Diameter Capital Partners, Redwood Capital and FourSixThree Capital bought about $190 million of Brightline’s municipal bonds from Nuveen this week, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Australia Housing Market: Why Are Home Prices Falling, How Far Could They Drop
summary: For the past three decades, Australia’s property market has experienced a prolonged boom, with prices rising sharply despite periodic downturns. In the past seven years alone, national house prices have risen by roughly 70%, resulting in one of the most expensive property markets in the developed world.

title: Paramount Wraps Up $52 Billion Debt Sale to Fund Warner Buyout
summary: Banks wrapped up the syndication of roughly $52 billion of debt to fund Paramount Skydance Corp.’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., locking in long-term financing at a hefty cost for the US media giant.

title: UMich’s Stevenson on Fed Report, Inflation Reading
summary: Betsey Stevenson said the Inspector General’s report finding no criminal wrongdoing in the Fed renovations confirms what many already suspected: the investigation was about a president pushing against the Federal Reserve’s independence. She argued Jerome Powell respected the institution’s need to stay separate from presidential influence because the Fed’s job is to keep prices stable and employment at maximum sustainable levels. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Why American Homeowners Are Stuck
summary: The gap between today’s mortgage rates and the low rates many homeowners locked in before 2022 is reducing moves and home sales. This is limiting the supply of homes for sale and contributing to higher prices, explains Bloomberg Opinion columnist Justin Fox. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: National Geographic Shares its 130+ Year Story
summary: Since first forming as a scientific club in 1888, National Geographic has evolved into one of the world's most recognizable magazines in the world. Chief Storytelling Officer Kaitlin Yarnall joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss National Geographic's news book which tells the 130+ year history of the organizations "legendary photographs, artifacts, adventures, and discoveries that changed the world."  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mexican Peso Becomes World’s Worst as Carry Traders Flee
summary: Analysts are rushing to cut their year-end forecasts for the Mexican peso after it underperformed every other major currency over the past month.

title: The Elusive Power Players Behind the Rise of Jane Street
